questions.q: What happens without exception handling if float('N/A') is called inside a loop processing many rows?
options: The error crashes the entire program, stopping processing of every remaining row
Python silently skips that row and continues
The value is automatically converted to zero
Nothing happens — Python ignores conversion errors by default
questions.explain: Without a try/except, one bad value can halt an entire batch job.

options: Runs the try block, and if a matching error occurs, jumps to the except block instead of crashing
Runs both blocks every single time, regardless of errors
Prevents any code inside it from ever running
Only works with numeric values, never strings
questions.explain: This is how Python catches an error and keeps the program running instead of stopping entirely.

questions.q: Why is catching a specific exception type (like ValueError) better than a bare except:?
options: A bare except: can accidentally hide a real, unexpected bug you actually needed to see
Specific exception types run faster with no other benefit
Bare except: is required by Python and cannot be avoided
There is no difference between the two approaches
questions.explain: Catching only what you expect to go wrong lets genuinely unexpected errors surface instead of being silently swallowed.

questions.q: What does the finally block do?
options: Runs no matter what happened in the try block — whether it succeeded, failed, or even returned early
Only runs if no exception occurred
Only runs if an exception did occur
Deletes the try/except block after one use
questions.explain: finally is useful for cleanup work, like closing a file or connection, that must happen regardless of outcome.

questions.q: What is the real pattern this lesson demonstrates for processing a list of raw values?
options: Wrap the risky conversion in try/except inside the loop, so one bad value gets skipped instead of crashing the whole job
Stop processing entirely the moment any bad value is found
Convert every value to a string before processing
Ignore all values and return an empty list always
questions.explain: This resilience — one bad row doesn't crash the whole job — is exactly what Lesson 27's ETL script needs.
